methodology: Real Three.js objects, production path/transition modules, actual custom OrbitControls, and production main lifecycle functions isolated in VM. Only DOM and renderer are simulated. This validates scheduling, geometry-independent camera continuity, state restoration, and sampler separation; it does not measure GPU performance or rendered image quality.

results.check: camera paths: exact visible endpoints and zero terminal velocity
near views at distance 5 through 7 have no added orbit or dolly
aperture begins transparent and ends beyond all viewport edges
prepare: actual draw scheduling, renderer restoration and no attachment feedback
prepare failure: restore temporary uniforms and support a clean retry
concurrent prepare shares work; disposal during async preparation prevents later draws
forward lifecycle at 30, 60 and 120 Hz commits once after final composite
production main integration: near-room return restores saved pose with one handoff
production mid-transition resize resolves latest destination and commits only once
return after viewport changed in gallery adapts saved room pose on first resolve
cancel before and near completion never commits or calls completion; restart remains usable
reduced motion uses a short dissolve without camera excursions and still commits once
long and invalid deltas cannot skip handoff or reverse transition progress
renderer state restores even if a source, destination or composite draw throws
target formats and final disposal follow capabilities without leaving active resources
production OrbitControls flush preserves the visible pose while clearing real residual inertia
